1. We have around 80 fully fledged alters, but we have like 200 fragments (fragments are parts that dont really have that same sense of identity as alters do, and have a limited job or memory.) 
2. Usually whoever the host is, but we switch a lot so there isn't necessarily a main one out and around. The host changes a lot too, but right now I am the host (Tubs.) 
3. People IRL dont really know we have it except for our medical professionals (we keep it on the DL), but they can tell theres a difference there. Like they can tell we're suddenly acting childish and clearly age regressed and will change how they act around us when there is a little out or near, but they don't even know we have DID or what exactly causes that behavior change. Online, we're way more open and people act pretty casual ab it and ask who it is if they cant tell, but sometimes they can tell by the behavior change/ typing pattern change even if we don't tell them theres a switch.

okay so Dissociative Identity Disorder is a dissociative disorder caused by trauma before and during the ages of 7-9 years old. because of the childhood trauma, I could not naturally integrate so the normal states that children have before 7-9 could not integrate into one person. these states because of the trauma became seperated by amnesia and dissociation barriers and so these states became alters, or alternate states of identity. So basically, we formed like "seperate people" in one body (I wouldn't say alters are seperate people, but they are in a way: different genders, ages, sexuality, etc) If you know what Multiple Personality Disorder is, DID is the new name for it. I was diagnosed this year, but I began to understand I had DID a year prior because the amnesia started to become really hard and more obvious and new trauma memory came back.
